title: Studying macrophage activation in immune-privileged lens through CSF-1 protein intravitreal injection in mouse model
protocol: Prepare equipment and laboratory space for injection.
Connect a glass micropipette to a holder for the Drummond Nanoject II Automatic Nanoliter Injector.
Stretch laboratory parafilm on the surface of a 35 mm × 10 mm cell culture dish.
Add 1 μL of sterile saline on top of the film.
Press the fill-model to fill the sterile saline into a glass micropipette.
Use the inject-model to test the count of 1 μL of liquid.
Anesthetize mouse by intraperitoneal injection of xylazine and ketamine cocktail (20 mg/kg xylazine, 100 mg/kg ketamine).
Add levofloxacin drops on the surface of the eye to prevent infection.
Insert a 33-gauge needle to make a hole approximately 1 mm behind the limbus at the superior temporal quadrant into the vitreous cavity.
Fill a glass pipette with 0.5 μL of CSF-1 solution.
Pull out the 33-gauge needle lightly and insert the filled glass micropipette into the hole made by the needle behind the limbus.
Inject reagent into the vitreous cavity using the Drummond Nanoject II Auto-Nanoliter Injector.
Gently remove the glass micropipette after injection.
Reapply levofloxacin drops on the eye surface to keep it wet and prevent infection.
Place the mouse on a heating pad until the mouse is awake and alert.
Fill a glass pipette with 0.5 μL of CSF-1 receptor antagonist (AFS98) solution.
Pull out the 33-gauge needle lightly and insert the filled glass micropipette into the hole made by the needle behind the limbus.
Inject reagent into the vitreous cavity using the Drummond Nanoject II Auto-Nanoliter Injector.
Gently remove the glass micropipette after injection.
Reapply levofloxacin drops on the eye surface to keep it wet and prevent infection.
Place the mouse on a heating pad until the mouse is awake and alert.
Fill a glass pipette with 0.5 μL of saline solution.
Pull out the 33-gauge needle lightly and insert the filled glass micropipette into the hole made by the needle behind the limbus.
Inject reagent into the vitreous cavity using the Drummond Nanoject II Auto-Nanoliter Injector.
Gently remove the glass micropipette after injection.
Reapply levofloxacin drops on the eye surface to keep it wet and prevent infection.
Place the mouse on a heating pad until the mouse is awake and alert.
Isolate the eyeball under a dissecting microscope 24 hours after CSF-1 intravitreal injection.
Place the isolated eyeball in PBS.
Make a hole approximately 1 mm behind the limbus using a sharp needle in PBS (same site of injection).
Fix the whole eyeball in 0.75% paraformaldehyde in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube for 24 hours at 22°C.
Place the tube on a shaker shaking at the lowest speed during fixation (∼60 rpm).
Pierce through the same hole made during the injection step.
Rinse off PFA with PBS three times, incubating for 30 minutes each time.
Incubate the eyeball in 10% sucrose for 1 hour at room temperature.
Incubate the eyeball in 20% sucrose for 1 hour at 22°C.
Incubate the eyeball in 30% sucrose for 12 hours at 4°C.
Embed the eyeball in Tissue-Tek® optimal cutting temperature compound (O.C.T.) in a sagittal position.
Dip the embedding mold in liquid nitrogen until the O.C.T. changes to a porcelain white color.
Store the embedded eyeball at −20°C for at least 12 hours before cutting sections.
Cut sections in a sagittal orientation at a thickness of 12 μm.
Mount the sections on prepared gelatin-coated glass slides.
Keep cut sections at −20°C until use.
Immerse the frozen tissue sections in cold acetone at −20°C for 2 min.
Air-dry the sections.
Draw a liquid barrier around each tissue section using Hydrophobic Barrier PAP Pen.
Rinse the slide with PBST to remove residual O.C.T..
Wash the sections with PBST three times, 5 minutes each time.
Add 0.1% Sudan Black solution at 22°C for 10 min.
Wash the sections with PBST three times, 5 minutes each time.
Incubate with the blocking solution at 22°C for 1 hour.
Add Rabbit inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) polyclonal antibody at a 1:100 dilution and incubate at 22°C for 1 hour.
Incubate overnight at 4°C.
Wash the sections with PBST three times, 5 minutes each time.
Incubate with donkey-anti-rabbit 647 secondary antibody at a 1:400 dilution at 22°C for 1 hour.
Wash the sections with PBST three times, 5 minutes each time.
Incubate with the blocking solution at 22°C for 1 hour.
Add goat Arginase-1 polyclonal antibody at a 1:300 dilution and incubate at 22°C for 1 hour.
Wash the sections with PBST three times, 5 minutes each time.
Incubate with donkey-anti-goat 488 secondary antibody at a 1:400 dilution at 22°C for 1 hour.
Wash three times with PBST, five minutes each time.
Add rat-anti-mouse CD68 polyclonal antibody at a 1:500 dilution and incubate at 22°C for one hour.
Wash three times with PBST, five minutes each time.
Incubate with donkey-anti-rat 594 secondary antibody at a 1:400 dilution at 22°C for one hour.
Wash three times with PBST, five minutes each time.
Add 4',6-Diamidino-2'-phenylindole (DAPI) at 1 ug/mL and incubate for ten minutes.
Wash three times with PBST, five minutes each time.
Mount the sample with Fluoromount-G.
Seal the edges of the cover slip carefully with nail polish.
Allow the nail polish to dry in a dark location for ten to fifteen minutes.
Store the slides in a black plastic box at 4°C to prevent quenching of fluorescence signals until imaging is completed.
Maintain tissue section slides hydrated during immunofluorescence staining.
Dilute all antibodies before use.
Keep solutions on ice.
Isolate the eye and observe refractive transparency in the injected right eye.
Compare refractive transparency between the injected right eye and non-injected left eye.
Discard samples if leakoma or lens injury is observed after injection.
Choose Cx50−/−/AQP0−/− knockout mice for the model due to congenital cataracts.
Ensure injective steps, especially the injection angle, are strictly followed in cases with congenital cataracts.
Isolate the eyeball carefully under a dissecting microscope 15 days after CSF-1 intravitreal injection.
Place the isolated eyeball in PBS.
Make a hole at a point approximately 1 mm behind the limbus using a sharp needle.
Place the entire eyeball into Fekete’s acid-alcohol-formalin fixation solution in a microcentrifuge tube.
Incubate the eyeball with shaking at the lowest speed (60 rpm) for 24 hours at 22°C.
Rinse off the fixation solution with 70% Ethanol directly.
Dehydrate the eyeballs with 70% Ethanol for 1 hour.
Dehydrate the eyeballs with 80% Ethanol for 1 hour.
Dehydrate the eyeballs with 95% Ethanol for 1 hour.
Repeat dehydration in 100% Ethanol three times, each for 1 hour.
Change to 100% Xylene and repeat three times, each for 1 hour.
Embed eyeball in paraffin wax at 58°C for 2 hours (repeat once).
Prepare sagittal paraffin sections of approximately 3-μm thickness.
Immunohistochemistry-stain with Monoclonal mouse anti-human α-SMA antibody at a dilution of 1:200.
Follow the manufacturer’s protocol using VECTASTAIN® ABC Kit for staining.
Perform antigen retrieval prior to immunolabeling the paraffin sections.
